reviews.title: Cancelled my paid subscription — security became an afterthought
reviews.text:
I've cancelled my paid subscription, and I want to explain why in terms of what I actually bought: a privacy service I trusted with my data.

The 404 Media investigation (Samantha Cole, "Reaping and Sowing: CEO Edition") documents a growth-at-all-costs culture at the top — an aggressive AI push over engineers' objections, and leadership dismissing a request to security-test new code before it shipped as "loser thinking." A culture that treats caution as the enemy of speed is a culture that will, sooner or later, cut the corners that keep your data safe. For a privacy product, that's not a values disagreement — it's a defect in the thing I'm paying for.

The software still works. That was never the problem. I just can't keep paying into a company where the growth culture now outranks the security I signed up for.

reviews.title: Serious concerns about the 4+ rating and parental controls
reviews.text:
I am very concerned that this vpn app has a 4+ age rating without sufficiently highlighting its potential impact on parental controls and children’s online safety. 
My son was grounded, and specifically prohibited from playing certain games on his tablet. However, he was able to download this app and use it to bypass the restriction that had been put in place, allowing him to access and play those games freely without my knowledge or permission. 
Parents rely on device restrictions and network security setting to help manage their children’s screen time and protect them online. An app rates suitable for children aged four and above should not be designed nor allowed to undermine these safeguards without clear warnings to parents. 
I appreciate that vpns have legitimate uses, but I believe the potential for children to use them to circumvent parental restrictions needs and o be taken seriously. 
I urge the developers and the App Store to review the age rating, introduce appropriate safeguards, and clearly inform parents that this app may allow children to bypass certain network level restrictions. 
Parents should not have to discover this the hard way. 
Please take parental concerns seriously and help ensure that the tools intended to protect children are not so easily circumvented.

reviews.title: App can’t handle changing networks
reviews.text:
**EDIT: Updated review after three months from two stars to one star because the app prompted me to review it and this issue is still not resolved.**

Disconnect from Wi-Fi -> internet stops working -> open Proton VPN to disconnect and reconnect vpn.

Connect to Wi-Fi again -> internet stops working -> open Proton VPN to disconnect and reconnect vpn.

Move within a building and the Wi-Fi switches to a different AP -> internet stops working -> open Proton VPN to disconnect and reconnect vpn.

Move a little too far away so the Wi-Fi signal gets weak and iOS starts using 5G Assist -> internet stops working -> turn Wi-Fi completely off -> open Proton VPN to disconnect and reconnect vpn.

I have tried different settings and just about every troubleshooting step. I used to use Mullvad VPN without any issues at all, now I have never been more aware of every single time my network even just gets a sniffle.

reviews.title: It’s alright
reviews.text: I switched to Proton VPN from ExpressVPN because of the supposed improved privacy of Proton. However, it’s very noticeably slower, and I get more connection errors while browsing web sites etc. Some features of apps do not work, and then work when I disable the VPN. I also find the app a bit over complicated for its own good. It has good design visually, but poor design from a layout and UX perspective: no search of countries / states when creating a profile; no ability to select multiple servers for 1 profile to choose the fastest among them (e.g. fastest server in one US state as a profile is not possible, but is possible when you search for the state); countries and their subdivisions are all in one list, etc. It could be more intuitive and easier to use. The only real simple use case is the “one tap connect” case, which basically applies to all VPN apps. Another issue: I exported a profile for use with my router as a VPN client. After a while it was suddenly connected through Germany, while before it was in a different country. This should not happen. Lastly: the app is pretty poorly optimized. A lot of obvious main thread work causes unnecessary hangups in UI rendering while loading etc. They should do better to keep loading off of the main thread. In general I expect better from an app like this, but here I am.

reviews.title: Used to work, now it’s breaks my internet when switching networks
reviews.text:
The ProtonVPN app used to work great on my iPhone 12 mini and now iPhone 17 Pro, but as of a few months ago, it has introduced a new severe issue.

As of the past 2-3 months, every time I am on my home network (Wi-Fi) and I connect to a ProtonVPN server on the app, then walk outside, disconnect from my Wi-Fi because I am out of range, my phone tries to switch cellular and the vpn just gets stuck saying “Connecting” in the iOS settings, and it never connects and there is no internet connection on the phone at this point. The only fix I have found to get a connection back is to go into iOS Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > VPN > Proton VPN > Delete VPN. Which is extremely annoying and defeats the purpose of an always-on seamless vpn service, especially when it used to work just fine before. I have seen a Reddit post on r/ProtonVPN mentioning the same exact issue on their iPhone 17 Pro, so it is not specific to my end.

PLEASE ProtonVPN support fix this issue!! It prevents me from using your service since it ceases to work anytime I switch networks which is way too often. This didn’t used to be an issue on my iPhone 17 Pro so it must either be a newer version of the ProtonVPN app that broke something or a new iOS update broke how VPN network hopping works.

reviews.title: CANNOT TRUST

You should avoid this app like the plague. Proton says you’re connected to a server in a country that you pick, but in reality, it’s just a virtual server and you’re connected to a different country.  I’m usually in Miami, even if I pick somewhere in South America. Lots of Asian countries default to Singapore. 

Proton’s customer service acknowledged this bug, can reproduce it, and as of a few days ago, said “we have no idea when it’ll be fixed”.  It’s been happening to me for 6 months now.  This is total BS for a premium service.  

CS team is pretty bleh.  They told me to try all the different connection types and play with setting to see if I can fix this myself.  So…even though they can easily reproduce this issue, their recommendation is for me to waste my time to see if I can fix the problem, with no real/clear direction.  At this point, the most efficient thing for me to do is find a new VPN provider.

reviews.title: Unusable
reviews.text:
I subscribed to Proton VPN Plus for a year, but the iOS app has a major issue with network switching. The VPN constantly doesn’t auto-reconnect when switching between WiFi and mobile networks, and when this happens, apps that require internet access, like Google Maps, Waze, WhatsApp, and email, stop working completely.

The only fix is to manually disconnect and reconnect the VPN, which is frustrating and time-wasting. I had to do this dozen of times a day. I gave up and ended up going back to NordVPN. Their support is also not very helpful.

This needs urgent attention – reliability on iOS isn’t there yet. I’d update this review if it improves.

reviews.title: Cancelling subscription after 4+ years.
reviews.text: This service has become a safety concern. Random disconnections from every server no matter the protocol with no indication (also, kill switch has now failed multiple times for the first time ever), pages crashing continuously, and unbelievably long load times when I am actually able to maintain a connection. Close your for phone for 30 seconds? Disconnects. On a server within your own city with the lowest server load? Disconnects (again no matter the protocol). UI is terrible now, US servers are all the way at the bottom of the list, and they removed the ability to immediately make profiles. If I’m browsing for over 10 min, I’m always checking to see if I’m suddenly reconnecting to the server, when I’ve never had this issue in the past. I’ve gladly paid $96 a year for the values Proton carries regarding data privacy, but this has become far too frustrating to keep paying for. It’s a shame, and I never leave reviews, but beware.

reviews.title: Good but “always-on” ruins it
reviews.text:
I took out a subscription for Proton VPN Plus for my home computers and decided to use it on my phone. In general the VPN works well however the phone app has a setting to ensure the VPN is always on which cannot be disabled “for your security”. It seems like a reasonable idea however I am concerned about an app removing my control of my phone in this way. The forced use of VPN interferes with the connectivity between my phone and other devices in my home. 

This makes me want to request a refund for my subscription and return to my old provider just to regain control of my phones network connection despite significant extra subscription costs

I would probably give a 5 star review if not for this.

reviews.title: Claims political neutrality but shows compromise
reviews.text:
I’ve used Proton products for a while because the core idea is solid: privacy-first, encryption by default, and a real alternative to Big Tech data harvesting. Where things get complicated is Proton’s claim of being “politically neutral.”

In early 2025, comments from Proton’s CEO — and briefly from official Proton channels — were interpreted as praising a specific U.S. political party’s stance on tech regulation. Those posts were later deleted and walked back, with Proton stating they didn’t reflect an official position.

This shows an inconsistency in their claims and practice, and gets you to truly question their legitimacy.

I love it for the most part but one major flaw makes me question whether to keep using it. This is not a one off occurrence and has happened many times, but Proton VPN essentially blocks all WiFi connections and the app cannot get past the load screen. This means I cannot turn off the VPN and is presumably continually trying to connect. Turning off the phone doesn't work, VPN from the Settings, and eventually have to delete the app and reinstall to fix it. I've had to do this enough times that I'm considering purchasing an extra VPN on top of my Proton subscription.

Update: Nothing has seemingly changed and seems to have gotten worse. It often says it's connected but stops all internet connections. If your phone dies with it on, guaranteed you have to disconnect from it and reconnect because, again, it stops all internet connections.

reviews.title: So Frustrating
reviews.text: Switched to Proton after finding out my other provider’s ’no logs’ policy wasn’t accurate. Unfortunately, unlike my other provider, ProtonVPN can’t automatically handle switching from cellular to WiFi or vice versa. For example, when I leave home and/or then return, I have to manually turn the VPN off then on again for it to work. Otherwise the phone won’t load anything! I snagged a 2-year membership for 60% off but unless they sort the auto switching issue out, I won’t be renewing - ‘no logs policy’ or not.
